title: Replace CDN links with GitHub Pages and modernize dictionary theme
description:
## Summary

The legacy `rsacdn.link` CDN is being retired. This repo now publishes via **GitHub Pages** (enabled on `main`, root). This PR repoints the data dictionary references to the Pages URL and removes the CDN-hosted styling from the dictionary source.

## Changes

- **Repoint data dictionary links (7 milestone files):** the `mdrd` dictionary now links to `https://rstudio.github.io/academy-tidyverse-renal-treatment/assets/mdrd_dictionary.html` instead of `rsacdn.link`.
- **Modernize the dictionary source:** `assets/mdrd_dictionary.qmd` was R Markdown (`output: html_document` + `cerulean` theme + a `teachthis` CDN stylesheet). It now uses native Quarto `format: html` with the default **cosmo** theme and `embed-resources: true` (self-contained single file, no external CDN assets).
- **Re-rendered** `mdrd_dictionary.html`.

## Verification

- `grep` confirms **no** `rsacdn`, `cerulean`, or `teachthis` references remain in any `.qmd` or `.html`.
- Dictionary re-rendered self-contained (no `_files/` sidecar).
- GitHub Pages enabled and building; live dictionary URL returns HTTP 200.

title: Remove broken factor-order exercise from data types milestone
description:

This removes the exercise and its now-orphaned solution image, and updates the section intro to match the remaining content.

title: Regenerate milestone01.png for current ggplot2 binning defaults
description:
## Problem

The milestone 1 solution image, `images/milestone01.png`, cannot be reproduced from `data/mdrd.csv` with a current ggplot2. Learners trying to recreate it found that no value of `bins` or `binwidth` in `geom_histogram()` would match the distribution shown, which is confusing when the whole task is "recreate this plot."

## The data was never wrong

Reading the bar heights straight out of the committed PNG:

- the bars sum to **1434** — exactly the number of `dropout == 0` observations in `data/mdrd.csv`
- the lone rightmost bar sits at the true `max(gfr)` of **58.44**
- the bin width is **1.9331**, exactly `diff(range(gfr)) / 29`

So the figure was generated from this same data set with the same default `bins = 30`. The values are unchanged.

## Cause: ggplot2 changed where default bins are anchored

ggplot2 4.0.0 reworked `bin_breaks_bins()` to anchor the default breaks at `boundary = x_range[1] - width/2`, centring the outer bins on the data minimum and maximum. Earlier versions anchored at `boundary = width/2` relative to zero.

The bin *width* is identical under both rules here. Only the *offset* moves — by 0.4469 — which shifts observations between adjacent bins and visibly changes the bar heights:

| | first bin edge | leading bar heights |
|---|---|---|
| ggplot2 3.x (committed image) | 0.967 | 1, 5, 21, 41, 77, 120, 157, **195**, 172, 180 |
| ggplot2 4.0.x (current) | 1.413 | 1, 9, 19, 57, 77, 134, 165, **198**, 164, 185 |

Because the anchor moved and the width did not, no `bins` or `binwidth` value can recover the old figure — which is exactly the reported symptom. Adding `boundary = width/2` to the current code reproduces the previous image's bar heights exactly, confirming the diagnosis.

## Fix

Regenerated the figure from `data/mdrd.csv` using the milestone's own solution code:

```r
mdrd |>
  filter(dropout == 0) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = gfr)) +
  geom_histogram()
```

Saved at the original **1344x960** (7x5in @ 192dpi), so the panel and axes land on the same pixels and only the bars change.

## Verification

- Bar heights read back out of the new PNG match `ggplot_build()` on the solution code exactly, across all 23 non-empty bins.
- `images/milestone02.png` needs **no** change and is untouched. Milestone 2 passes an explicit `binwidth = 0.1`, which takes a code path this ggplot2 change did not affect; confirmed it still reproduces pixel-for-pixel.

## Note

The regenerated image reflects ggplot2 4.x defaults. Learners installing packages from CRAN per the README will be on 4.x, so this is correct for them; anyone still on ggplot2 3.x would see the older binning.
